Second destination for the mission payload, $3EF0 bytes.

comments.text: Twenty consecutive 64-byte sprite slots in VIC bank $4000. Each slot begins with 21 rows of three pixel bytes, and the last byte is outside the displayed height.
Four sprite slots after the first sixteen mission frames. The VIC slot positions relative to bank $4000 are $A0-$A3.

Four rows of four character codes per 16-byte tile. The map renderer resolves a tile ID through the resident screen-code pointer tables, then indexes this pattern with the character coordinates modulo four.
Tile dictionary slots for IDs $40-$7F in the mission 5 dictionary. Entries are 16 bytes apart.
The dictionary reaches the final tile ID $99 at $C990. The stage tile maps select from this address band for their higher tile IDs.
Tile-indexed colour bytes. The initial playfield renderer at $17CD reads these in parallel with the tile character pointers and $1882 writes the chosen value to colour RAM.
Primary 256-character graphics source. The resident wipe routine at $1DC2 enables RAM under I/O and copies the selected pixel rows to the live character set at $4000.
Rows for character codes $80-$FF in the main stage's 256-glyph set. The masked copy selects them through the same eight-byte stride as the lower codes.
Alternate 256-character graphics source in RAM below the I/O window. The resident wipe routine chooses this source when $1902 is set, unless the alternate scene flag $ADF7 takes priority.
The upper half of the alternate stage's eight-byte character slots, read under CIA and expansion register addresses with I/O banked out.
Stage 1 grid, 64 entries per row and first 9 rows. Each byte selects one 4 × 4 character tile through the split table at $08D6/$09C6.
Stage 1 grid, 64 entries per row and first 9 rows. The engine uses the low three bits for world-coordinate attribute lookups and modifies the grid during play.
Stage 2 grid, 64 entries per row and first 9 rows. Each byte selects one 4 × 4 character tile through the split table at $08D6/$09C6.
Stage 2 grid, 64 entries per row and first 9 rows. The engine uses the low three bits for world-coordinate attribute lookups and modifies the grid during play.
Stage 3 grid, 64 entries per row and first 9 rows. Each byte selects one 4 × 4 character tile through the split table at $08D6/$09C6.
Stage 3 grid, 64 entries per row and first 9 rows. The engine uses the low three bits for world-coordinate attribute lookups and modifies the grid during play.
Stage 4 grid, 20 entries per row and first 7 rows. Each byte selects one 4 × 4 character tile through the split table at $08D6/$09C6.
Stage 4 grid, 20 entries per row and first 7 rows. The engine uses the low three bits for world-coordinate attribute lookups and modifies the grid during play.
Sixteen 64-byte source slots that the bootstrap at $F7C8 transfers to $6440. The mirror routine generates further frames in live sprite storage from this copy.
Installs sixteen sprite frames from $F080 at $6440. Then mirrors frames from the end of the new region into two more slots.
Copies X pages from the source pointer in $CA/$CB to $6440, advancing both pointers a page at a time.

Reverses both the three bytes of each of 21 rows and the order of pixel pairs within each byte. Uses the reversal table at $0600 and advances the source and destination pointers to the next 64-byte slots.
The one-based mission number used for this file and for play selection in the resident engine.
Four split pointers with their high bytes at $FCC5. The resident loader at $0B26 selects a stage and gives its grid to the row-pointer builder at $0B46.
Four split pointers with high bytes at $FCCD. The grid parallels the tile map and the resident coordinate lookup at $3DFA masks each attribute to its low three bits.
Stage widths used as a byte stride for the tile and attribute row pointers.
Stage heights used by the resident scaler to derive the vertical playfield limit and by $8EAD to walk the attribute grid.
Indexed stage values copied to $2D during setup by $0AFD.
VIC extended background register $D022 values selected by stage.
VIC extended background register $D023 values selected by stage.
Indexed initial view value written to $1781 before the character drawing loop at $1785.
Four split pointers with high bytes at $FCED. $8FE8 copies 128 bytes from the selected source into a separate workspace half for each player.
Indexed stage bytes cached at $0AEA and $0BE0 before display setup.
Stage index compared at $1A82. A match enables the alternate source at $D800 and installs the two operand bytes following this value at $1642/$1643.
Four indexed values. Stage setup at $0B0E copies the selected value to $1901.
The pair at $FCFC/$FCFD supplies the two operand bytes at $2B0A/$2B0B.
Low and high bytes of the mission-provided routine that $1AB3 calls after preparing the stage grids.

Stage 1 placement seed copied into player workspace by $8FE8. A record has a destination low byte, destination high byte and value. A zero value ends the loop that applies records to the working stage grid.
Stage 2 placement seed copied into page $0200. The resident setup applies the value of each record at its two-byte destination and stops at the first zero value.

Placement records shared by stages 3 and 4 in this mission, with an in-game destination word followed by a value byte. The loader supplies $70 bytes of this workspace source before the overlay ends at $FEEF.
